did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah describes a punishment in which the bones of the kings of Judah, the officials, the priests, the prophets, and the people of Jerusalem will be brought out of their graves.
Did you know? The bones will be scattered before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven—the very powers the people loved, served, sought, and worshiped—and they will not be gathered or buried.
Did you know? The devastation will be so great that the survivors who remain will prefer death to life in every place to which they are exiled.
Did you know? Jeremiah describes Jerusalem as having continually turned away, clinging to deception and refusing to return from its path.
Did you know? The prophet compares the people to migrating birds: the stork, dove, swift, and crane know the times of their migration, but the people do not know the judgment of the Lord.
Did you know? The claim, “We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us,” is invalid when the scribes’ pen distorts what is written; therefore, their boastful wisdom loses its value.

Did you know? Jeremiah accuses the prophets and priests of pursuing dishonest gain and practicing deceit, describing corruption as a problem that affects the entire society—from the least to the greatest.
Did you know? The leaders of the people try to heal their brokenness with the shallow claim, “Peace, peace,” even though there is no true peace.
Did you know? The enemy is described as coming from the north on warhorses, whose snorting and neighing make the whole land tremble; they consume the land and its inhabitants.
Did you know? Alongside the image of a military enemy, Jeremiah uses the image of venomous snakes for which there is no healing charm, expressing a calamity that cannot be escaped.
